correctness.rationale: Parikh lower bound and terminal clash force length >=2pn+1. At that length, a terminal-letter split reduces membership to two boundary-separation conditions. Every marked postboundary opposite letter deletes exactly once; a minimum-milestone-count contradiction proves the inverse inserts all 2(n-1) letters before the last unmarked one. Thus the bijection is valid for all p,n>=2. Actual standalone tests passed 84 DP cases, 14706 bridges and 5960 brute words; no finite test substitutes for the written proof.

evidence: Lin establishes a general inequality bounding the shortest-supersequence count by C(a+b,a); after setting a=b=h it reads C(2h,h).
The supplied construction attains that ceiling for both p,n>=2 and supplies an explicit inverse, which the inequality alone cannot establish.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A universal upper bound does not imply that these particular highly overlapping inputs attain it. An arbitrary-input generation algorithm can enumerate the answers but does not itself state their number or the equality characterization.
